notes:
User collects vintage cameras and postcards and has resumed postcard collecting; they now have added 25 postcards since restarting, noting rapid growth. They plan to organize postcards by theme, maintain a digital catalog, and start with a simple postcard rack. Their catalog template uses description, date, publisher, condition, acquisition date/source, and unique ID; possible additions include image description, back message/caption, postal history, and provenance. Known examples: PC001 1920s Paris postcard, unknown publisher, excellent/minor edge wear, acquired 2 months ago from a local antique shop; PC002 vintage beach scene, 1950s, Colourpicture Publishers, near mint, acquired 1 month ago on eBay; PC003 Eiffel Tower at Night, 1960s, unknown publisher, used/slight crease, acquired 2 months ago from a local antique shop. They also bought 8 postcards at a local antique shop.

For vintage cameras, they like space-saving displays, especially wall-mounted shelves, and may combine these with glass-fronted cases. Other ideas include shadow boxes, acrylic/Lucite risers, and rotating stands. They asked about film-development learning resources.

They are excited to host a collector gathe
